newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil portworkers wait for May 13 in pay dispute.
newsitem.headline: Brazil portworkers wait for May 13 in pay dispute.

text.p: Workers at Brazil's port of Santos are not considering any industrial action until they see whether the CODESP port authority fulfills its promise to pay outstanding April salaries on May 13, union officials said.
"We agreed to wait until Tuesday (May 13) and in the meantime we'll take some legal action," said Francisco Bertozzi, vice-president of the Administrative Portworkers Union.
"Until then, I am advising that we do not strike. We have to wait until Tuesday," he said.

Workers yesterday refused to work at public terminals in protest at receiving only 65 percent of last month's salary which CODESP said was due to a cash-flow problem caused by a four-day stevedores strike in April.
The port authority yesterday deposited the remaining 35 percent of basic salaries but could only pay part of additional performance-related monies which 30 percent of the workforce normally receive.
At a prolonged meeting last night between port authority officials and union representatives, CODESP promised to pay the outstanding salaries on May 13.
Given yesterday's stoppage was not an official strike, workers returned to work today and the port is functioning normally, a port spokeswoman said.
Santos is Brazil's largest coffee exporting port and also handles sugar, wheat, orange juice and soyproducts.
